caveats: Market capacity (p) for metros comes from brokers (CBRE, Cushman & Wakefield) and mostly measures third-party colocation/wholesale inventory; owner-operated hyperscale campuses are partly or wholly excluded (esp. Northern Virginia). Treat as a lower bound on total IT capacity. CBRE and C&W figures are not strictly comparable (different market boundaries and dates).

u values derived as (1 - vacancy) measure LEASED capacity, not average power draw. The only metered calibration found is Ireland: CSO 7,663 GWh (2025) vs KPMG 1,543 MW installed IT -> u*PUE = 0.567. Using occupancy (~0.95) x PUE 1.56 (~1.48) instead would overstate energy ~2.6x. Consider u*PUE ~ 0.57 as a cross-market default where no metered data exist.

PUE: no public market-level averages for most metros; Uptime's 2024 global industry average (1.56) is used as a placeholder (regional breakdowns are paywalled). Hyperscaler campuses (Google 1.04-1.17 TTM) sit far below this, so blended PUE is likely lower in hyperscale-heavy markets (Dublin ~88% hyperscale, N. Virginia).
Google per-site PUE is from datacenters.google (Q2 2026 TTM); Google does not disclose per-campus MW or electricity, so p for The Dalles and Council Bluffs is null.
Abilene is changing fast: ~200 MW IT operational (Apr 2026) vs 1.2 GW planned by end-2026; the value is likely stale by Sep 2026.

Ulanqab p is derived from standard-rack counts (2.5 kW/rack); AI racks draw far more than 2.5 kW each physically, but the 'standard rack' is already a power-normalised unit, so 1,250 MW is built capacity; built is not energised (73% occupancy in 2024).
Manufacturing sites (Zhengzhou, Taoyuan) and AI-lab offices (SF, Seattle, London, Beijing) have no sourced load figures; only population is filled.

Population uses official metro/urban-area definitions as a proxy for 'within ~100 km'; notes flag where the true radius would be materially larger (London, Sao Paulo, Singapore+Johor, Taoyuan+Taipei).

Some broker pages were read via fetch summaries rather than full PDFs; figures cited from CBRE GDCT 2026, C&W APAC (Mar 2026), CSO, KPMG, the Dominion/PJM letter and Google were confirmed on the source pages.
